title: ephemeral-storage-pressure-workflow-and-debug-playbook
content:
Summary:
This is a living runbook draft + incident retrospective for transient cluster instability caused by ephemeral (node-level) storage exhaustion on a subset of worker nodes. Symptoms were slow pod scheduling, high scheduler queue length, kubelet eviction cycles, and downstream request latency for a small set of latency-sensitive services (routing, embeddings API). No data loss; partial degradation for ~23 minutes.

Severity & Impact:
- Severity: Sev2 (service degradation, partial customer impact).
- Scope: ~8/120 worker nodes in us-west-2 cluster; ~120 pods delayed/stuck Pending or CrashLoopBackOff during peak.
- Services affected: routing-proxy (intermittent 5xx), batch-transform jobs delayed.

Detection / Alerts that fired:
- alert: NodeFilesystemLow available bytes (Grafana) on node pool workers-ssd-1 - 03:12 UTC
- alert: kubelet_eviction_in_progress on same nodes - 03:15 UTC
- alert: scheduler_queue_length > 100 (5m aggregate) - 03:16 UTC
- Slack: #oncall paged by pagerduty at 03:18 UTC (pager: eng-sre)

Initial hypothesis:
- Nodes ran out of ephemeral storage (/var/lib/kubelet or imagefs) causing kubelet to throttle pod starts and perform eviction/GC; scheduler backlog grew while kubelet struggled to reconcile. Secondary hypothesis: a noisy batch job wrote excessive logs or image pull caches grew due to failed GC.

Timeline (UTC):
- 03:12 - First NodeFilesystemLow alert for workers-ssd-1-03 and -07.
- 03:14 - kubelet_eviction_in_progress alert for same nodes.
- 03:16 - Scheduler queue length crosses 100. Ops triage begins.
- 03:18 - Oncall confirms many pods in Pending + Recent Kubelet events show "failed to create pod sandbox: no space left on device".
- 03:21 - Investigative commands run (see below).
- 03:25 - Emergency mitigation: cordon + drain of two most impacted nodes after manual cleanup frees space.
- 03:32 - Scheduler queue begins to drain.
- 03:35 - Remaining nodes cleaned via DaemonSet cleanup job; kubelet restarts on 3 nodes.
- 03:45 - Alerts recover. Post-incident noise continued for ~10 minutes as rollouts progressed.

Investigation notes (use these commands when triaging):
- Quick checks:
  - kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels
  - kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide | head -n 40
  - kubectl describe node workers-ssd-1-03 | egrep -A3 "Non-terminated Pods|Capacity|Allocatable"
  - kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 200
- Disk and kubelet specifics (ssh to node if necessary):
  - df -h /var/lib/kubelet /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/docker
  - du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/* | sort -h | tail -n 30
  - journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | egrep -i "evict|no space|imagefs|rootfs|failed to create pod sandbox"
  - crictl images --digests | awk '{print $3,$6,$7}' | sort -hr -k3 | head -n 40 (containerd)
- Scheduler & api-server checks:
  - kubectl get --raw /metrics | grep scheduler_queue_length_total (or check Grafana)
  - kubectl top nodes
- Runtime GC/containers:
  - crictl ps -a --no-trunc | grep "Exited" | wc -l
  - ls -lah /var/log/containers | head -n 50 (rotated logs can pile up)

Root causes we observed in this incident:
1) A misconfigured batch job (weekly-log-collector v2.4) created large temporary archives under /tmp on the host via hostPath mounts. The job used ephemeral hostPath without cleanup on failure.
2) Node-level log rotation was not configured for the container runtime logs; old logs accumulated over ~2 weeks due to a change in the logrotate config (PR #312 introduced a path mismatch).
3) Container image garbage collection (kubelet) parameters were too conservative for this pool: imageGCHighThresholdPercent left little headroom when image pulls spiked during a failed deployment.

Mitigation (immediate) - oncall playbook (ordered):
1) Identify worst nodes: kubectl get nodes --selector=nodepool=workers-ssd-1 -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{@.metadata.name}:{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}\n'
2) SSH / run remote cleanup (preferred safer operations):
   - sudo systemctl stop kubelet (only if cleanup requires space and kubelet is blocking)
   - sudo rm -rf /var/log/containers/*-old-logs-*.log (limit to >14d)
   - sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/pods/*/volume*/ | sort -hr | head -n 20 (identify large hostPath usage)
3) If safe, cordon + drain the node to reduce scheduler pressure: kubectl cordon $NODE; kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
4) Launch emergency cleanup DaemonSet (one-off): a privileged pod that deletes stale archives in /tmp and prunes unused images (containerd) on nodes matching the label; manifest stored in k8s-ops repo.
5) If nodes do not recover after cleanup, restart kubelet (sudo systemctl restart kubelet) to re-evaluate image GC and eviction.
6) After nodes healthy, uncordon: kubectl uncordon $NODE

Playbook command examples (copy/paste with care):
- Bulk cordon for impacted pool:
  for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=workers-ssd-1 -o name); do kubectl cordon $n; done
- Drain single node quickly (emergency):
  kubectl drain workers-ssd-1-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=3m
- Emergency remote cleanup (careful, test on a single node first):
  ssh ops@workers-ssd-1-03 'sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/* | sort -h | tail -n 20; sudo rm -rf /var/log/containers/*.log.1; sudo systemctl restart kubelet'
- Deploy cleanup DaemonSet: kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redwood-inference/k8s-ops/master/runbooks/ephemeral-cleanup-ds.yaml

Observability & metrics to monitor (dashboards to check):
- node_filesystem_avail_bytes for /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/containerd (Grafana panel)
- kubelet_eviction_count and kubelet_eviction_in_progress
- kube_pod_start_time_seconds histogram (tail rising shows startup stalls)
- scheduler_queue_length (5m/1m) and apiserver_request_duration_seconds 95p
- crictl image sizes / count (exposed via node-exporter custom exporter)

Short-term remediation actions (post-incident):
- Fix the weekly-log-collector job to delete temp archives on failure and not use hostPath or to use a size-limited PVC. (PR created: #312)
- Revert/patch logrotate mismatch that prevented rotation of container logs.
- Raise imageGCHighThresholdPercent for workers-ssd-1 pool from 85 -> 90 (config roll planned).
- Add a periodic DaemonSet to prune old images and rotate logs for 30d retention.

Long-term changes / follow-ups (owners & tickets):
- INFRA-874: Add automated tests that simulate disk-pressure and validate our eviction thresholds and imageGC behavior (owner: Diego).
- INFRA-879: Add a Grafana alert for sustained scheduler_queue_length > 75 for >5m (owner: Michael).
- SRE-EPHERMAL: Document an official ephemeral-storage runbook on Confluence; include safe cleanup commands and escalation matrix (owner: Asha).
- k8s-ops#312: merge the logrotate fix, add CI lint that ensures logrotate matches runtime paths.

Known gotchas & safety notes:
- Deleting files under /var/lib/kubelet/pods/* can cause kubelet to behave unpredictably; prefer deleting large hostPath artefacts created by known job names or log files in /var/log/containers.
- Restarting kubelet can temporarily increase scheduler backlog; cordon before restart if you expect long restarts.
- Be careful with --delete-local-data during drain; it will remove local-dir data for pods that rely on it.

Oncall escalation & contacts:
- Primary SRE oncall: eng-sre pager duty (at time of incident: Riley Thompson)
- Infra lead: Diego Alvarez (pager)
- Developer of weekly-log-collector: Priya Singh (Slack @priya)

Post-incident summary (TL;DR):
A combination of a noisy batch job using hostPath and a mismatched logrotate config caused ephemeral storage to fill on a small subset of workers. Kubelet evictions and blocked pod sandbox creation caused the scheduler queue to spike. Immediate cleanup + DaemonSet and targeted kubelet restarts restored capacity. Action items: fix job, patch logrotate, tune imageGC thresholds, and add detection for sustained scheduler queue length.

Edit history:
- 2025-11-18: initial draft (Asha Patel)
- 2026-01-16: added timeline and mitigation commands after runbook dry-run (Michael Chen)
- 2026-02-09: incorporated INFRA-874 ticket links and cleaned up steps (Riley Thompson)

Notes to self / open questions:
- Should we move weekly-log-collector to a batch nodepool with larger local disks or force it to use an NFS/PVC?
- Can we expose image GC metrics per node in Prometheus to detect preconditions earlier?

Appendix: quick recovery checklist (copy for incident page)
1) Verify alerts and identify impacted nodes.
2) Cordon worst nodes.
3) Launch emergency cleanup DaemonSet.
4) If needed, SSH + remove old container logs (>14d) and temporary archives.
5) Restart kubelet only after cordoning; monitor scheduler.
6) Uncordon nodes once node metrics stable for 3m.
7) Create follow-up tickets, update Confluence runbook.

End of document.
